correctness.rationale: Selected cells are edges in a complete bipartite incidence graph. Occupancy >=3 gives a rook triangle; if every incidence degree is at most two the components are paths/even cycles, whose line graphs are bipartite. For maximality, any row and column both of degree <=1 must already meet in a selected cell. If both deficient classes are nonempty this forces exactly one of each, both of degree one at the common cell, and 2m-1=2n-1. Otherwise a whole shore is of degree two, necessarily the smaller shore on a rectangle. The independent labeled-column monomials thus count exactly the rectangular class. On a square the two classes consist of a spanning simple bipartite two-factor, or an isolated selected incidence at one of r^2 pairs plus a two-factor on the remaining board. Alternating cycles on j specified labels on each shore number (j!)^2/(2j) for j>=2, giving the claimed exponential function, the r=2 exception (A_1=0) and both sizes for r>=3. For a_r=A_r/(r!)^2, the singular expansion gives a_r=e^(-1/2)(pi r)^(-1/2)(1-3/(8r)+O(r^-2)); the next coefficient transfer is valid for the analytic remainder multiplying (1-t)^(3/2). Dividing consecutive terms and using a_{r-1}/(a_r+a_{r-1}) yields 1/2+1/(8r)+O(r^-2) for uniform sampling of labeled sets. An independent six-board replay of graph maximality, two-colorability and the coefficient counts matched both boundary and nontrivial cases, including B_3,4=114z^6 and B_4,4=96z^7+90z^8.
residual_risks: Finite board checks do not prove the all-order claim or the asymptotic.
The probability concerns uniform labeled sets, not greedy generation or unlabeled orbits.
